claims.text: An Al-based high-entropy alloy can provide lightweight and superior comprehensive performance compared with conventional alloys.
The base alloy is Al10Co25Cr8Fe15Ni36Ti6 and is produced by vacuum induction melting.
The alloy is modified by adding 0.5 at.% Hf to Al10Co25Cr8Fe15Ni36Ti6.
The modified alloy is processed by directional solidification, such as the Bridgman process.
The alloy can be annealed at 900 °C for 50 h.
Tensile testing is performed from room temperature to 900 °C under a controlled deformation rate.
Hf modification produces sharper corners on the γ′ precipitates.
Hf modification produces a controlled, reduced volume fraction of the Heusler-type phase.
Directional solidification refines the alloy's grain structure.
Hf-modified precipitate morphology promotes stronger and more reproducible γ′-phase formation.
Hf suppresses detrimental effects associated with a high-volume Heusler-type phase.
Directional solidification minimizes weak grain-boundary orientations.
The alloy's aluminum content provides a low-density or lightweight profile.
Directional solidification increases UTS and reduces variability relative to conventional casting.
The proposed combination of Hf modification, directional solidification, and heat treatment enhances ductility.
The proposed alloy and processing combination improves high-temperature oxidation resistance.
The Hf-modified alloy will have significantly higher tensile strength and ductility than the unmodified alloy.
The Hf-modified alloy can attain UTS values exceeding those of comparable conventional alloys such as Inconel 617.
The Hf-modified alloy will exhibit improved microstructural uniformity.
Conventionally cast and annealed Al10Co25Cr8Fe15Ni36Ti6 has lower strength and greater mechanical-property variability than directionally solidified material.

contradictions.description: The stated baseline is an unmodified alloy made by conventional casting and annealing, whereas the falsification experiment uses an unmodified control processed under conditions identical to the directionally solidified Hf-modified samples. These are different controls, so the intended comparison is inconsistent.
